name: Episodic Ataxia Type 5

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Episodic Ataxia Type 5

criteria.description: Recurrent episodes of cerebellar ataxia lasting minutes to hours
Identification of pathogenic mutation in the gene associated with EA5 (e.g., SLC1A3)
Normal or mildly abnormal neurological examination between attacks
Exclusion of other causes of episodic ataxia and paroxysmal neurological disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent episodic ataxia plus genetic confirmation of pathogenic mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis; clinical presentation alone is insufficient due to overlap with other episodic ataxias.

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes of ataxia
imaging: Brain MRI usually normal or may show mild cerebellar atrophy in long-standing cases

distinguishingFeatures: EA1 presents with brief episodes of ataxia lasting seconds to minutes
EA1 often includes myokymia, which is absent in EA5
EA2 episodes last longer (hours to days)
EA2 associated with interictal nystagmus and progressive ataxia

redFlags: Progressive cerebellar degeneration outside of episodic attacks
Severe persistent neurological deficits between episodes
Family history of early-onset neurodegenerative disorders
references: Jen JC, Wan J, Palos TP, Howard BD, Baloh RW. Mutation in the glutamate transporter EAAT1 causes episodic ataxia, hemiplegia, and seizures. Neurology. 2005.
Klockgether T. Episodic ataxia. Handbook of Clinical Neurology. 2018.
